title: Plan 2 drafted from roadmap (status:draft)
body: Drafted Plan 2 per docs/roadmap-2026-05-19-install-ux-architecture-v0.md (v1.2). Four-feature shape per roadmap §Plan 2: F001 declarative PrereqProbe + 5 profiles + JSON (ship-fast, independently shippable); F002 dontpanic init interactive + --non-interactive; F003 dontpanic smoke synthetic dispatch; F004 HTML install report. Forbidden_decisions explicitly carve out the operator review constraints: no auto-PAT-create, no auto-SA-key, no Firebase requirement for --profile=core, no `maintainer` profile in v0 (defers to Roadmap Plan 5/7), no Windows v0. Cross-feature invariants pinned: backwards-compatible doctor (no-flag path preserves 0/1/2 exit-code matrix), no silent failures, network-bounded preflight (<=10s wall clock, 2s per network probe in ThreadPoolExecutor), dual-channel output (pretty + JSON), safe-by-default auto-install (opt-in per probe). Status:draft awaiting operator review before lock. Dependencies declared on Plan 3 (schema fix landed at commit c104c22 — doctor strict-validate would have false-failed without it).

title: Pre-lock review pass — 1 blocker + 6 high-risk + 4 medium resolved
body: Operator review of D001 draft surfaced 1 blocker + 6 high-risk design issues + 4 medium issues. All addressed in this revision; plan revalidated against schema. BLOCKER (objective_contract validation): Added required completion_test field; removed out_of_scope_for_v0 and merged into non_goals (matched the schema's allowed property set). HIGH-RISK FIXES: (1) Doctor default behavior contradiction resolved — `dontpanic doctor` (no flags) keeps legacy CheckResult pipeline + existing probe set + 0/1/2 exit-code matrix UNCHANGED; new profile-aware path activates ONLY on --profile=<name>; `dontpanic init` defaults to --profile=core (not doctor). (2) Profile model: pseudo-profiles like core-when-auditor-codex eliminated. Profiles are frozenset[str] of probe names; conditional severity lives on per-probe activation_condition enum (always | github_remote_present | auditor_codex_selected | dispatch_requires_push | firebase_target_set) + severity_when_inactive enum (omit | advisory | warn). (3) Codex CLI: advisory under --profile=core unless activation_condition.auditor_codex_selected resolves true; FAIL under ci+openclaw always. NOT a blanket core blocker. (4) GitHub auth: warn under --profile=core when github_remote_present resolves true, OMIT when no github remote, FAIL under --profile=ci. NOT a blanket core blocker. (5) Smoke split: `dontpanic smoke --mode=mocked` (v0) validates supervisor plumbing only; real-CLI presence validated by doctor probes, NOT smoke. MockExecutor.is_available() bypasses real-CLI lookup. --mode=live deferred. (6) 'Every supervisor branch' eliminated — acceptance NAMES exact surface set: plan load, gate eval, mocked executor envelope write, audit JSON persist, signoff envelope write, INBOX append, tmpdir cleanup. MEDIUM FIXES: (a) Plan 4 architecture.json dependency removed from motivation + non_goals; install UX is independent of architecture map. (b) 'full sweep >=2036' replaced with 'no regressions vs lock-time baseline' (no hardcoded count). (c) doctor --json envelope carries explicit top-level schema_version='1.0.0'; local schema doc at evidence/doctor-json-envelope-schema-v1.md; formal agent-conventions promotion deferred. (d) F002 auto-fix: strict argv allowlist (subprocess.run(argv: list[str], shell=False)); validator rejects shell-string fix_command at startup; package-manager installs OFF by default (auto_install_safe=False default); no --auto-fix-safe-all batch flag in v0. ALSO: --profile-strict flag namespace chosen instead of --strict to avoid clash with Plan 3 F003's --validate-plans-strict / Plan 4 F003's --architecture-drift-strict precedent (commits c104c22 + 6032046). objective_contract.json now validates clean against v1.0 schema.

title: Pre-lock review pass 2 — 1 high contradiction fixed + per-profile severity policy hint
body: Operator review pass 2 (after D002 revision). HIGH FIX: objective_contract.json line 45 had a stale acceptance_signal saying `--auto-fix-safe-all flag opts into batch execution` but line 105 + features.json F002 say NO --auto-fix-safe-all in v0. Resolved by changing line 45 to `Each auto-fix prompts operator per-probe by default; no --auto-fix-safe-all batch execution in v0`. All three artifacts now consistent (greps verified). SECONDARY CAUTION (not a lock blocker — implementation guidance): F001's severity model (required_for_profiles + activation_condition + severity_when_inactive enum) may not be expressive enough for the stated cases — gh-auth wants 'warn under core, fail under ci' and codex wants 'advisory under core, fail under ci/openclaw'. Recommendation for implementer: use an explicit per-profile severity policy (e.g. `severity_by_profile: dict[str, Severity]`) rather than forcing everything through a single `severity_when_inactive` enum. The single-enum model may need to grow into a per-profile map during F001 implementation; that's expected churn, not a re-litigation. Acceptance criteria are clear enough that either model satisfies. Plan now lockable: clean schema validation + explicit completion_test + concrete user journeys + bounded F001 ship point + no Firebase-in-core leakage + smoke/mock separation + strict-argv auto-fix discipline + auto-fix-safe-all contradiction resolved.

body: Locked Plan 2 via `dontpanic plan lock` with operator-authored sufficiency-findings.json (auditor=operator, empty findings, substantive _operator_note pointing at D002+D003 review). Same precedent as Plan 5 D003: operator review (D002 fixed 1 blocker + 6 high-risk + 4 medium; D003 fixed the auto-fix-safe-all contradiction + flagged per-profile severity hint) serves as the sufficiency analysis. F001 dispatching in parallel with Plan 5 F002 — disjoint file scopes (Plan 2 F001 touches scripts/dontpanic_doctor.py + new prereq_registry + tests; Plan 5 F002 touches docs/showcase/README.md + repo README pointer + scripts/showcase.sh + Makefile + new test file). README.md is in both allowed_paths but Plan 2 F001's substantive scope doesn't need it; theoretical-only collision.

title: F001 close-out: stopped_no_progress (3 findings hand-patched at close)
body: Plan 2 F001 terminated stopped_no_progress after 2 rounds (iter0+iter1 both needs_changes). Three findings all hand-patched at close-out rather than re-dispatched: (1) HIGH/test_coverage — added test_no_flag_text_output_byte_identical_against_mocked_results in test_doctor_profile_integration.py that monkeypatches doctor.run_all_checks to return a deterministic CheckResult list (one PASS, one WARN, one FAIL exercising all render_text branches) and asserts the exact rendered string + legacy exit code 1. Pins byte-identity of the legacy no-flag text output against pre-F001 snapshot, removing the host-state coupling that prevented the original implementer from writing this assertion. (2) MEDIUM/test_coverage — added test_aggregate_five_profile_sweep_under_10s_budget in test_prereq_registry_f001.py with the timer wrapping the full five-profile loop (instead of starting inside it). Aggregate finished at 2.76s in dev — operator-init walkthrough latency invariant is now real. (3) MEDIUM/documentation — updated docs/plans/2026-05-19-002.../evidence/doctor-json-envelope-schema-v1.md exit_code row to align with implementation: 0 = all probes PASS *or* only ADVISORY, 1 = at least one WARN, 2 = at least one FAIL. Clarified that ADVISORY is informational (per-probe activation_condition resolution surface) and never escalates exit code; pointed at SweepResult.exit_code() in prereq_registry.py as the source of truth. Full sweep 2120 passed / 7 skipped (+14 vs lock baseline of 2106 — the new snapshot test + aggregate timer + implementer's profile-integration suite); sanitization clean (1366 files). Operator-resolved as implementation_defect.
